newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans close higher on exports, harvest.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans close higher on exports, harvest.

text.p: Active exports and prospects for a weather-related slowdown in harvest this week in the U.S. Midwest boosted CBOT soybean futures to a higher close, traders said.
"The inspections are keeping the market firm. There continues to be good demand," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.
USDA Monday said 27.474 million bushels of soybeans were inspected for export during the week ended October 24, above trade expectations for 22 million to 25 million bushels.
Traders also said the prospects for slower soybean harvesting boosted prices.
Meteorologists said early Monday that corn and soybean harvest in the U.S. Midwest will likely be slowed again this week as a rain system moves across the area Tuesday.

"Tomorrow, we should see a rapid increase in cloudiness and there will be rain, probably during the morning," said Joel Burgio, meteorologist with Weather Services Corp. "The rainiest weather will be in west sections of the (corn) belt."
"The wet weather will delay harvest and there was a lot of bear spreading," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds.
Soybeans closed 1-3/4 to eight cents per bushel higher, with November up 1-3/4 at $7.02-1/4.

After the close Monday, USDA released its updated weekly harvest progress report, showing 73 percent of soybeans had been harvested in the United States as of Sunday, versus 63 percent a week earlier and 81 percent average. The figure was just under the 75 to 80 percent traders had been expecting.

Friday's Commodity Futures Trading Commission Commitments of Traders report showed non-commercials, including funds, were long soybeans 130.210 million bushels and short 97.250 million as of October 22. The tally for longs was down 77.105 million bushels from October 8 and the short total was up 29.080 million since October 8.
"They also were buying beans and meal on encouragement from Friday's CFTC report that showed a sharp reduction in the number of longs," said Mark Cermak of O'Connor and Co.
Technicians were eyeing resistance in the November at $7.05-1/2 a bushel and $7.17-1/2 and support at $6.93-1/2 and $6.81-1/2.
The session high for November was $7.06 and the low was $7.01.
"Beans and meal were supported by the strong technical performance last week," Cermak said.
The long term moving averages remained bearish for the market and the short term nine day relative strength index was edging back toward neutral territory with the November closing at 43.566 points.
An RSI of 30 or less is generally viewed as an oversold market and 70 or more as overbought.

Key players included Cargill Inc with five million bushels bought in the November, Continental Grain bear spread four million January/November and Cargill bull spread four million November/January, traders said.
Soybean futures volume was estimated at 57,000, down from 77,094 Friday, according to the CBOT.
In soybean options, The Chicago Corp sold 300 January $7.50 puts at 52 cents, Term Commodities bought 200 January $7.25 puts and sold 400 January $7.00 puts at even money, traders said.
Soybean options volume was estimated at 15,000 up from 8,781 Friday, the CBOT said.
